title.en: 이다 vs 아니다 and 있다 vs 없다

sub.en: Identity (to be / not to be) vs Existence & Possession (to exist / not to exist, have / not have)
sub.ko: 신분·정체 표현(이다/아니다)과 존재·소유 표현(있다/없다) 완벽 구분

desc.en: Free printable Korean worksheet comparing 이다 (to be), 아니다 (to not be), 있다 (to have/exist), and 없다 (to not have/exist): grammar rules, particle pairings, contrast tables, practice exercises and an answer key.

title.en: Identity vs Existence: The Four Fundamental Verbs

rows: 저는 의사가 아니에요. (I am not a doctor.)
To not exist / To not have
지갑에 돈이 없어요. (I have no money.)
sections.note: Crucial rule: 이에요/예요 connects directly to the noun with NO particle. In contrast, 아니에요, 있어요, and 없어요 all require the subject particle 이/가.
Pronunciation: 아니었어요 is pronounced [아니어써요], 있었어요 is pronounced [이써써요], 없었어요 is pronounced [업써써요].

title.en: How to Choose Between 이다/아니다 and 있다/없다

sections.text: Ask yourself what the sentence describes: If you are explaining WHAT a person or thing IS, use Noun + 이에요/예요 (or 이/가 아니에요 for negative). If you are describing WHERE an object is located or WHAT someone OWNS/HAS, use Item + 이/가 (장소에) 있어요/없어요. Remember: never say '안 이에요' (use 아니에요) and never say '안 있어요' (use 없어요).

howto: Distinguish identity sentences (what something is: 이에요/아니에요) from existence/possession sentences (where something is or what you have: 있어요/없어요).
Pay attention to particles: 이에요/예요 attaches directly without a particle; 아니에요 and 있어요/없어요 always require 이/가.
Complete Practice A to C and verify each sentence with the answer key.
